title: In 82 opto-tagged mouse visual cortex Neuropixels sessions, spike-train troughs confirmed rare Vip inhibition from slice data, but Sst-to-FS inhibition exceeded the slice prediction
abstract: We tested whether cell-class rules of local inhibition from slice recordings appear in awake spike trains. We used Allen Visual Coding Neuropixels (28 Pvalb-, Sst- and Vip-Cre;Ai32 sessions, passive viewing) and Visual Behavior Neuropixels (54 Sst- and Vip-Cre;Ai32 mice, task). Units were opto-tagged Pv, Sst or Vip, or untagged fast-spiking (FS) or regular-spiking (RS). For 1.57 million ordered unit pairs on the same probe within 400 micrometres, we tested cross-correlograms for a trough at 1-5 ms and a peak at 0.5-3.5 ms, and compared class-pair rates with Allen Synaptic Physiology slice connection rates. Troughs were class-specific: 8.3% and 6.9% of pairs with an inhibitory presynaptic unit, 0.6% with an RS presynaptic unit. As slice data predict, tagged Vip units rarely inhibited RS or FS units (adjusted odds 0.34 and 0.17 times those of FS units), and FS units rarely inhibited tagged Sst units. In contrast with slice data, which show no target preference, Sst units gave relatively more troughs onto FS than onto RS targets, while FS units did the opposite (interaction log odds +0.96 and +1.09). This difference stayed in early-trough and no-synchrony variants, but the Sst absolute preference then fell to near zero. Pv and Sst outputs onto RS units had similar adjusted trough rates, while slices show a twofold difference. Spearman correlations of in vivo with slice rates were 0.55 and 0.87 (0.33 and 0.65 after control subtraction). Short-latency peaks onto interneurons were as frequent from inhibitory as from RS presynaptic units, so peak tests do not identify excitatory inputs here. Limitations: small tagged Pv and Vip samples, waveform-based FS/RS labels, possible disynaptic or masked troughs, and a slice reference that is not distance-matched.

display.caption: Mean baseline-normalized spike cross-correlograms onto RS (left) and FS (right) target units, by presynaptic class, in Visual Coding (top) and Visual Behavior (bottom). Inhibitory presynaptic classes give a trough at 1-5 ms (grey band) onto RS targets; RS presynaptic units do not. Vip troughs are shallow. Peaks at negative lags show the reverse excitatory drive.

In vivo trough rate minus control-window rate for each inhibitory class pair against the Allen Synaptic Physiology slice connection rate (FS mapped to Pvalb, RS to excitatory). Bars are 95% intervals (mouse bootstrap in vivo, Clopper-Pearson in slice). Vip outputs are rare in both preparations; Sst-to-FS lies above the trend in both data sets.

Log odds ratio of a trough onto an FS target versus an RS target for each presynaptic class, adjusted for detection power and distance, with 95% intervals clustered by mouse. Circles: primary; squares: troughs before 3 ms; triangles: pairs without zero-lag synchrony. Black diamonds: slice Pvalb-target vs excitatory-target log odds ratio.
